steps.en: What you see: The cava runs as a straight thin walled tube into the right atrium. Normal Doppler steps forward twice per beat with a small backward wave when the atrium squeezes.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Right atrial pressure reads near 3 mmHg when the inferior cava is 21 mm or less with collapse above 50 percent.
Systolic reversal in systemic venous flow marks severe tricuspid regurgitation.
Loss of the forward waves with a dilated non collapsing vessel suggests obstruction or tamponade physiology.

Pitfalls: Catheters and leads throw bright echoes that fake masses; follow any line to the skin entry or chamber tip. In tamponade venous flow falls sharply with inspiration, so record through a full breath.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Aorta mistaken for the cava, the vein collapses and the aorta does not. Correct it by pressing lightly and watching pulsation, since the aorta kicks while the vein breathes.
Innominate vein mistaken for the cava from too high a window. Correct it by following the vessel into the atrium, since the innominate joins above it.
Off axis sample that damps the venous trace. Correct it by realigning until the walls are parallel and the trace sharpens.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at right supraclavicular fossa, sagittal toward the right atrium.
Point the probe marker toward the head, about twelve o clock.
Sit above the right clavicle and aim sagittal toward the atrium. Keep the beam within 20 degrees of the flow for a clean trace.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Spot obstruction and high right atrial pressure patterns.

q.en: Where does the probe sit for the superior cava view?

o.en: Right supraclavicular fossa aiming at the atrium

why.en: The right supraclavicular fossa lines up the cava with the atrium.

q.en: Systolic reversal appears in the venous trace with a dilated cava. What is likeliest?

o.en: Severe tricuspid regurgitation with raised atrial pressure

why.en: Reversal plus plethora marks severe regurgitation with high pressure.

q.en: A bright line runs the length of the vessel to the skin. What is it?

o.en: Catheter or lead, not a mass

why.en: Lines that track to an entry point are hardware, so follow them out.
